propositions: MCP transition_ticket and claim_ticket signatures omit write parameters (force, reason, caused_by, ref) already supported by the library and CLI, making those operations unreachable over MCP.

FastMCP derives JSON schemas and argument models from handwritten callable signatures in _mcp_writes.py, so undeclared payload keys are discarded before execution; the adapter forwarding independently omits the same values, requiring fixes at both the signature and delegate boundary.

The MCP adapter must expose transition force (str | None), caused_by (str), ref (optional str), and claim force (str | None), and forward each parameter unchanged to the shared library core (rebar.transition and rebar.claim).

Operator ruling 2026-08-18 rescinds the prior force-only-CLI policy; force is now allowed through all surfaces (library, CLI, MCP) with absent certification as the audit signal, and force_close remains unavailable.
